title: The Earth-Moon-Sun System
seo_title: Grade 8 Moon Phases, Eclipses and Seasons Worksheets: The Earth-Moon-Sun System
standard_text: Develop and use a model of the Earth-sun-moon system to describe the cyclic patterns of lunar phases, eclipses of the sun and moon, and seasons.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on the Earth-Moon-Sun system (NGSS MS-ESS1-1): the eight Moon phases, solar and lunar eclipses, and how Earth's tilt causes seasons. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Phases, eclipses and seasons follow cycles.
key_sub: Moon phases come from seeing more or less of its sunlit half. Eclipses need a line-up. Seasons come from Earth's tilt.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Sun always lights half of the Moon. As the Moon orbits Earth (about 29.5 days), we see different amounts of that lit half: the phases.

Eclipses: a solar eclipse happens when the Moon is between the Sun and Earth (new moon); a lunar eclipse happens when Earth's shadow falls on the Moon (full moon).

Seasons come from Earth's 23.5° tilt. The hemisphere tilted toward the Sun gets more direct sunlight and longer days, so it has summer.

Example

First quarter today. Phase in one week?

Two steps forward.

Answer: full moon

Example

Which phase can have a solar eclipse?

The Moon must be between the Sun and Earth.

Answer: new moon

Common mistakes

  • Thinking Earth's shadow causes the phases. It causes only lunar eclipses.
  • Thinking summer happens because Earth is closer to the Sun.
  • Thinking there is an eclipse every month.

faq.q: What causes the phases of the Moon?
faq.a: Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun. As the Moon orbits Earth, we see different amounts of the lit half.

faq.q: What is the difference between a solar and a lunar eclipse?
faq.a: In a solar eclipse, the Moon blocks the Sun from Earth. In a lunar eclipse, Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.
Earth's axis is tilted 23.5°. The hemisphere tilted toward the Sun gets more direct sunlight and longer days, so it has summer.

items.q: In December, it is winter in the Northern Hemisphere, where Sam lives. What is the main reason?
c: Earth is farthest from the Sun at that time.
The Sun gives off less energy in December.
That hemisphere is tilted away from the Sun, so sunlight hits it at a lower angle and days are shorter.
items.e: Seasons come from Earth's 23.5° tilt, not its distance from the Sun.
